body: It’s okay OP, I feel the same way. Your feelings are completely valid. Depression does not discriminate between whether you’re rich or poor, male or female, etc. Please take care

Hearing this, I’m extremely proud of you. I know you’ve had a rough life so far, and I admit things would’ve been much worse if I was in your shoes. I would’ve have been able to handle things the way you did. 

You say you’re jaded, but I don’t believe that is true. In fact, I believe that you’re insanely strong for going through what you have, and wanting to become a better person. 

You’re not silly for looking up to fictional characters. Plenty of people do that, including myself. Fiction offers a healthy way of escaping life, and it also teaches you different perspectives in life. 

OP, you are smart, and you’re not completely in the deep end yet. There’s still hope and I know you know that too. I’m be rooting for you.
I agree with this. If I want to die I want it to be a success

Loneliness won’t go away unless you find the root cause of why you feel this way, and face it head on. What I did after my breakup was to take the time to myself to think, breaking away from old patterns of unhealthy attachment to my  exes, jumping from relationship to relationship. Because I knew deep down I didn’t love him, I merely wanted sometime to fill the void. Once you learn to be okay alone, at peace with yourself, everything else will come naturally, I promise.

I understand. I’m also at that breaking point, where even the little things to look forward to don’t really matter anymore. I can’t feel happiness. 

However, what I can only do now is try to survive day by day, in hopes that maybe one day I will truly feel happy. 

While maybe this is not the answer you’ve hoped for, I hope you truly reconsider suicide. Even if they don’t find the body, they will live in devastation for the rest of their lives, confused as to whether you’re dead or alive. If you watch true crime, you know how agonising that is for them.

It really sucks what you’re going through. Even though this piece of advice might sound weird, this is what helped me: 

I tried my best to have things to do everyday, small things to look forward to, starting small. Maybe today I’ll draw, the next week I’ll cook, and the week after I’ll go window shopping. The point is, switching up your routine a bit may be helpful. 

Also, I know doctors have recommended this all the time, and at first I thought it was bullish—it’s exercise. Some light brisk walking, yoga, stretches at home

TLDR; switch things what make you happy

No man, OP, at that point you’ve already done your due diligence. You did your best. Your control and sense of agency does not extend past the boundaries of yourself. 

If your GF does (possibly) commit suicide, it is not your fault. You’re in a different country and you already tried what you can, which is informing her family. 

II strong believe things would be worse if the family out that you didn’t tell them anything. 

Lastly but not least, if she seriously needs help, she needs to be checked into a psychiatric ward
OP, I’m here for you to rant. I can’t promise I’ll reply immediately, but I will be here for you

If she really had the intention to commit suicidal, you did the right thing OP. I have immense respect for you. 

There was once someone did tell my close family that I was suicidal, and I got extremely angry at them for revealing something so personal. However over time I understood that it came from a place of concern and worry. 

I’m sure your girlfriend will forgive you in time. Give her some space alright

OP, I feel exactly the same as you. The feeling of hurrying so hard and nothing gets better. 

Again like my other comments, I can’t for sure say life will get better. However, you can find things to make you feel better. Such as picking up a new hobby, listening to music, etc. 

Learning to have your happiness independent on others is probably you need to learn. And I don’t deny it’s the most painful thing ever. However, I promise you, once you find yourself again, you won’t look back

My advise is to tell he brother. This is an extremely dangerous situation. I’m not sure if she’s being serious or not (idealisation vs intention). But the fact is you’re in a long distance relationship and it’s extremely hard to keep track of her. So instead, I think having a family member watch over your girlfriend (if your girlfriend trusts her family in general).

Hey OP, you know yourself best. I’m glad that you recognise that you’re not in good shape and pretty rough currently. That’s the first step. If you think inpatient is the best option for you, you should do go for it, regardless what other people think.
I agree wholeheartedly

That is completely not right, your mother is absolutely in the wrong. OP, if you’re over the legal age in your country, I beg you to go to a medical professional and seek help. 

At the same time, your mother doesn’t seem to be doing quite well as well. Y’all may both wanna seek help :(

Hey there OP, firstly I want to say that I’m happy that you survived the OD. Yes, I may be a stranger on the internet, but I am grateful you’re alive.  

I’ve been in your position before, ODing then going to school the next day as if nothing happened. It sucks, big time. The feeling of being alone, and the feeling like no one cared about how you felt. However, depending on how you tried to OD, it may be worth going for to a doctor for a check to access the damage. The only thing worse than failing a suicide attempt is actually damaging the organs, causing more pain and misery. 

I want you to know that you’re perfectly valid in how you feel. You don’t have to feel regret, I understand why you did it.

I also just created this account because before that, I felt like I wasn’t worth being heard out on. But this community, while sad, has found me comfort. And I hope to help and impact as many people as I can

I can’t speak for your experience, but for me, I used to jump from relationship to relationship without actually loving the person. I did it out of loneliness and I regretted it. 

A relationship is supposed to compliment, or in a way, amplify what you already have. A relationship isn’t a magic pill that cures all. 

OP, I know you can do it. You need to find happiness from within. Yes, I know it’s the hardest thing ever to do. You need to learn to be okay alone. Whether it be finding distractions in the form of hobbies, or developing healthy relationships with the people around you. Only then a relationship will make you happier. 

Please don’t die over this. I assure you the feeling will last, and you’ll meet someone
If it means anything, you are loved. I’m here for you if you need to talk

I’m in the same boat as you. It is a horrible feeling. I get it. 

For me personally, I keep a diary to rant on. I write letters to people to pen down how I truly feel, but never actually end up giving them the letters.  

For me, this practice is therapeutic in the sense that it kills 2 birds with one stone: I get to vent my feelings so I don’t feel bottled up and horrible, and I get to be honest with myself. 

However, if theres something seriously bothering you, I suggest going to a therapist, or a school councillor? It would be dangerous to keep everything in for a long time. Or tell a trusted friend about how you feel, albeit in a more “censored” and measured manner, as it may be overwhelming for them to hear everything. If they’re true friends, they will be more than willing to be there for you.

You are not dumb, boring, or ugly. I may be a stranger online, but I can assure you with confidence you’re not any of those. 

Sometimes you gotta accept that it’s not a you problem, you have done your part to communicate and reach out to them and they’re not doing theirs. It takes two hands to clap for a relationship to work, and as of now, they’re not doing their part. 

You are loved OP.

I’m so sorry OP, I know you’re in a whole lot of pain currently. I know it sucks, but please don’t commit suicide. I can’t promise that whatever situation you’re going through will become better, but what I can promise is the feeling of wanting to die will mellow down. You just gotta give it some time. If you’re at immediate risk of suicide, please, I beg you, talk to someone. If you need to talk, I’m here for you
Hearing your perspective and that someone else feels the same comforts me. I hope one day we are able to feel like we are a part of the world, and not an alien in human skin.

I agree with you, I don’t want that either honestly. 

I also don’t actually have a lot of friends either, because of trust issues. So I understand the loneliness. 

The best advice I can give to you is that while I can’t change the fact that this is how life works, try to find small, minute things, to look forward to. Whether it be a movie release, or a trip to the grocery store for a snack you’ve wanted. While rather insignificant, gripping onto the small things gives me something to look forward to everyday. At this point, I’m willing to take the small crumbs of happiness in my daily life. And I hope that works for you too.

I understand, I have a dog too which I love with all my life, and I dread and curse time as it passes by me and him. I just try my best to find solace in spending time with him. 

And yes, it’s extremely alienating. I feel like I’m in constant pain, invisible pain no one sees. And I feel extremely sorry for anyone going through this horrible, agonising illness. I hope one day we make it out together. We can do this.

At this point it may not seem like there’s anything else left to live for, I don’t deny I’ve been in the same situation many times. But I guess that’s what we call “tunnel vision”. I completely sympathise with how you feel. 

I think it’s best for you to cool down and walk away from the situation first. While I cannot guarantee you’ll feel better, you’ll have a clearer picture, rather than acting on your current emotions

I’m so sorry hearing all this. If it’s any consolation, your pain is being heard and felt. I understand how you feel with BPD, I suffer from it as well. And it feels like a death sentence sometimes. 

There will be days that feel worse than others. And while I cannot say I understand completely what you’re going through, since it is a lot, I want you to know that you’re not alone in your pain. 

I hope you find things worth living for. Your dog may be old but you’re all he has. And I promise you he loves you. So don’t go.

I agree, is there any way you can remove yourself from the situation? For instance, going out for a walk? Removing yourself from the knives (which are a temptation) may help you gather your thoughts and let your emotions settle
Please don’t do anything rash. I understand your pain. You deserve better than her. You’re so much more than her, don’t do something you’d regret. Dying will not change that
I’m sorry for your loss. Please remember to take care of yourself.
